source.title: When a Flatness Proxy Is Not a Function: Robustness Certificates and Training Interventions
source.authors: Vicente Opazo; Jose Calatayud-Mateu; Cristóbal Rojas; C. B. Calderon

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether flatness-based training interventions produce grokking-like delayed generalization. Its long-horizon results report inconsistent selective delay and no observed required onset separation in the modular-addition raw runs, qualifying the claim rather than reproducing its full pattern.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's long-horizon generalization results and its paired test of whether changing the raw-proxy gauge changes grokking onset. The certificate counterexample, proxy-value and gradient-invariance tests, and one-step update comparisons do not measure delayed generalization and are not rows for these versions. The study does not test gradual circuit formation, training-set-size dependence, or optimizer/numerical artifacts.
record.test_reason: The study uses grokking as a setting that separates memorization from generalization. It tests whether a flatness-proxy regularizer (Han et al. 2025) is gauge-identified and whether it causally suppresses or delays generalization. The delays are induced on purpose by the regularizer. The modular-addition 'onset separation' compares regularized and control onsets rather than measuring grokking arising on its own. No result bears on whether any grokking version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors' main conclusion is that a valid curvature upper bound does not justify use as a robustness certificate (a counterexample shows over 210× underestimation) or as an intrinsic training intervention. The raw proxy is gauge-dependent and gives function-equivalent models different updates, while row-centering (quotient) restores identification. The long-horizon results show reversible CIFAR-10 suppression but inconsistent selective delay, leaving open whether exact relative flatness is necessary.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses interventions based on raw and quotient relative-flatness proxies, plus CIFAR-10 long-horizon training and paired gauge changes; it does not reproduce the original small-dataset grokking recipe or sweep training-set size.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome depends on the proxy parameterization (raw versus quotient) and the training condition; CIFAR-10 suppression and recovery include a scheduled optimizer change, and some modular-addition onsets are unobserved by step 100000.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing only the function-null common-row coordinate (raw proxy about 100× its control) leaves grokking onset identical in all five modular-addition pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A gauge-dependent raw relative-flatness proxy value does not determine grokking onset.

fits_no_version.finding: A raw relative-flatness regularizer suppresses CIFAR-10 test accuracy by 10.61 points on average, and accuracy recovers by 11.90 points after removal. Selective delay after memorization is met inconsistently: 1/3 released seeds and 1/5 and 2/5 for the quotient variants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flatness-proxy regularization can induce reversible suppression of generalization, but does not reliably produce grokking-like selective delay after memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: In long-horizon modular-addition runs, no raw-regularized run shows the required 3000-step onset separation from controls; three onsets are unobserved by step 100000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Raw relative-flatness regularization does not reliably delay grokking onset in modular addition.

record.problems: The text reports aggregate run counts and ranges rather than uncertainty estimates or per-run trajectories. CIFAR-10 recovery follows both regularizer removal and scheduled optimizer changes. The modular-addition onset results include right-censored runs, and the text does not give the assignment of the two endpoint fractions to the quotient variants.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. Certificate analyses, gauge-proxy values, and one-step update tests were omitted because they do not measure delayed generalization or its onset.

untested.parts: Not tested: no measurement of the train/test accuracy gap timing or of dependence on training-set size.
Not tested: the CIFAR-10 delays are regularizer-induced; no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation of natural delay.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' with V1 and V3 labels is not supported: every long-horizon delay is caused deliberately by a flatness regularizer and is evaluated against the Han et al. causal-flatness claim, not against grokking as such. The study is not an original source. All rows are relinked to none.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests long-horizon results on modular addition but does not test whether delay grows as training data shrink, nor report the full chance-to-near-perfect test-accuracy trajectory described in the claim.
The CIFAR-10 experiments bear on delayed generalization outside algorithmic data, but do not test initialization scale, a lazy-to-rich transition, or the full set of modalities named in the version.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 raw-regularized runs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Train with the raw proxy regularizer; compare with paired cross-entropy controls before regularizer removal.
rows.measure: Test-accuracy difference from paired CE control
rows.value: Raw-regularized models trail by 10.61 percentage points on average (range 7.04–16.58).
rows.note: The result shows suppression, but by itself does not establish selective delay after memorization.
rows.check: Test-accuracy suppression is induced deliberately by the raw-proxy regularizer, measured against a CE control. It is not grokking-like delay arising from the training regime, so it does not bear on V3.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 raw-regularized runs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Remove the regularizer and apply scheduled optimizer changes.

conditions.value: after regularizer removal and scheduled optimizer changes

rows.note: The recovery phase also changes the optimizer schedule, so the result does not isolate regularizer removal.
rows.check: Recovery follows regularizer removal plus scheduled optimizer changes. This is an induced intervention effect, not a V3 measurement.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 raw-regularized runs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate whether runs satisfy the study's composite endpoint for selective delay.

conditions.value: memorization plus required ten-point test gap

rows.measure: Runs that memorize but do not reach the required test gap
rows.value: Three runs memorize without reaching the required ten-point test gap.
rows.note: These runs do not meet the study's selective-delay endpoint.
rows.check: This row records failure of the study's own selective-delay endpoint for an induced regularizer effect. 'Absent' is relative to the Han et al. causal claim, not to a grokking version.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 raw-regularized runs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate whether runs satisfy the study's composite endpoint for selective delay.

conditions.value: memorization plus required ten-point test gap

rows.measure: Runs that reach the test gap without memorizing
rows.value: Two runs reach the gap without memorizing.
rows.note: The test gap occurs without the memorization prerequisite in the study's endpoint.
rows.check: Reaching the test gap without memorizing is not the reverse of any version's effect; 'reversed' is a mislabel. The effect is also regularizer-induced.

rows.subject: Released CIFAR-10 loop (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Run the unchanged released training loop.
rows.measure: Runs satisfying the same composite endpoint
rows.value: Suppression and recovery occur in all three seeds; only one satisfies the same composite endpoint.
rows.note: The text does not provide separate numeric suppression and recovery values for these seeds.
rows.check: Released Han et al. loop with an induced regularizer; same issue as r1–r4.

rows.subject: Modular-addition raw-regularized runs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measure grokking-onset separation in long-horizon runs.
rows.value: No observed raw run shows the required 3000-step onset separation; three raw onsets remain unobserved by step 100000.
rows.note: Some onsets are right-censored at step 100000, so their eventual separation cannot be determined.
rows.check: The 3000-step separation is between raw-regularized and control grokking onsets, a test of the regularizer's causal effect. It does not measure V1's delay after training-accuracy saturation. Some onsets are right-censored at step 100000.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 quotient-regularized variants (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Train with quotient-proxy variants and evaluate the composite endpoint.

conditions.value: quotient variants; variant-to-fraction assignment not stated

rows.value: The quotient variants satisfy the endpoint in 1/5 and 2/5 runs.
rows.note: The text gives two fractions but does not identify which fraction belongs to which quotient variant.
rows.check: Quotient-regularizer endpoint fractions measure an induced intervention, not a version of the claim.
